title: Beyond Calabrese-Cardy Scaling: Exceptional-Point Sensitivity from the de Sitter RT Surface
abstract: Entanglement entropy at one-dimensional criticality typically follows the Calabrese-Cardy scaling. In non-Hermitian critical chains near exceptional points, however, we show that the biorthogonal entropy of a finite system retains an additional sensitivity to a small energy gap \(Δ\) even when \(Δ< 1/L\). On top of the usual Calabrese-Cardy term, we find an interval-independent contribution \(S_{\rm res}=\log(ΔL)\), visible as a vertical offset and detectable even for a one-site subsystem. This behavior has no Hermitian analogue: a sub-finite-size gap is effectively invisible to entanglement in unitary critical chains, whereas here the entropy continues to resolve such a gap through its dependence on \(ΔL\). We interpret the result within the de Sitter geometry generated by non-unitary continuous multiscale entanglement renormalization: because the dS extremal surface reaches the IR endpoint, entanglement necessarily retains the endpoint contribution. On a finite ring, a regular circuit cannot terminate at a one-site product state and instead leaves an entangled two-site IR state. Computing the entanglement of the IR state recovers the same \(\log(ΔL)\) term, identifying this additional long-range entanglement as the residual entropy left after finite-depth disentangling.
summary: The paper shows that entanglement entropy in non-Hermitian critical chains near exceptional points acquires an extra residual term proportional to $\log(\Delta L)$. This unique feature arises because the underlying physics generates a de Sitter geometry, forcing the entanglement calculation to sense the system's finite energy gap ($\Delta$) in a way that Hermitian systems cannot.
main_problem: To investigate entanglement entropy scaling beyond standard Calabrese-Cardy predictions, specifically revealing an additional sensitivity to a small energy gap ($\Delta$) in non-Hermitian critical chains near exceptional points (EPs).
main_result: Non-Hermitian criticality introduces a residual entropy term, $S_{	ext{res}} = \log(\Delta L)$, into the entanglement entropy that is absent in Hermitian systems. This term signifies long-range entanglement left over after finite-depth renormalization group flow.
method: The analysis uses entanglement entropy as a probe, comparing holographic descriptions derived from Anti-de Sitter (AdS) vs. de Sitter (dS) geometries generated via continuous MERA renormalization group flow.
model_or_system: The study focuses on non-Hermitian critical chains, exemplified by the two-legged nH Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) model. The comparison is drawn between unitary (AdS) and non-unitary (dS) quantum field theories.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy ($S_A(\ell)$), residual entropy term ($\log(\Delta L)$), and the gap ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: System size ($L$), subsystem length ($\ell_A$), and the small energy gap ($\Delta$) near the exceptional point.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending cMERA to non-unitary critical states, generating an emergent dS geometry whose extremal surface reaches the IR endpoint.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how the entanglement entropy scaling differs between AdS (where the RT curve bypasses the singularity) and dS (where geodesics reach the singular IR core), leading to a measurable vertical offset in the latter case.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the standard Calabrese-Cardy scaling, then introduces non-Hermitian criticality near an EP. It develops the holographic connection by comparing AdS/dS geometries and uses cMERA flow analysis to derive the residual entropy term $\log(\Delta L)$ from the IR endpoint structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum critical points in non-Hermitian systems, linking topological features (like gap sensitivity) directly to emergent spacetime geometry (dS vs. AdS).
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
